definitions.definition: For integrable f, Fourier(f)(k) = fhat(k) = (2 pi)^(-1) integral_0^{2 pi} f(x) exp(-ikx) dx; extend by distributional duality.

For real s, H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with norm squared sum_{k in Z} <k>^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are distributions. L2=H^0 with normalized measure. On mean-zero distributions dot H^s has squared norm sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2. Smooth means spatially C-infinity. Real means fhat(-k)=conjugate(fhat(k)), and mean-zero means fhat(0)=0. Sequence ell2 uses counting measure. Time L-infinity norms are essential suprema, except time suprema of continuous representatives. Generic constants C may change; C_M depends only on gamma,T,M, never on a Fourier support bound or timestep.

argument.text:
Fix four nonnegative ell2 sequences, under temporary antecedent L1.  It suffices first to consider finitely supported sequences. Decompose into shells \(2^j\le|k|<2^{j+1}\), \(j\ge0\), set x_{r,j}(k)=x_r(k)1_{2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1)}, and write \(Xshell_{r,j}\) for the \(\ell^2\) norm of the \(r\)th sequence on the \(j\)th shell. Fix an ordering of the four shell indices \(j_1\ge j_2\ge j_3\ge j_4\). A nonzero zero-sum interaction has \(j_1-j_2\le2\). For each fixed pair of smaller-shell frequencies, the remaining sum of the two larger-shell sequences is at most their \(\ell^2\) norm product by Cauchy–Schwarz, since one sequence is a translated reflection of the other. Sum the smaller frequencies in \(\ell^1\). A shell has at most \(2^{j+1}\) integer elements, so another Cauchy–Schwarz bound gives
\[
\sum_{a+b+c+d=0}\prod_{r=1}^4 x_{r,j_r}
\le C2^{(j_3+j_4)/2}\prod_{r=1}^4 Xshell_{r,j_r}.
\]
Since \(N_3\ge2^{j_3}\), the weight leaves \(C2^{-(j_3-j_4)/2}\). For \(q=j_1-j_2\in\{0,1,2\}\), extend the nonnegative sum by dropping the upper restriction on the smaller shells. The contribution is at most
\[
C\left(\sum_{J0} Xshell_{1,J0}Xshell_{2,J0-q}\right)
\left(\sum_{\ell\ge m}2^{-(\ell-m)/2}Xshell_{3,\ell}Xshell_{4,m}\right).
\]
The first factor is bounded by Cauchy–Schwarz. Writing \(r=\ell-m\), the second is at most
\[
\sum_{r\ge0}2^{-r/2}\|Xshell_3\|_{\ell^2}\|Xshell_4\|_{\ell^2}
=\frac{\|Xshell_3\|_{\ell^2}\|Xshell_4\|_{\ell^2}}{1-2^{-1/2}}.
\]
Sum over at most 24 orderings and three offsets. For arbitrary nonnegative sequences apply the finite bound to their restrictions to \(|k|\le m\). The infinite positive sum is the supremum of these finite sums, while the norms of the restrictions are bounded by the full norms. This proves the infinite statement without exchanging conditionally convergent sums. 
Restriction to a subset only decreases the nonnegative sum. Discharge L1 to obtain the universally quantified output.
